As previously described, the process of immortalization (*amṛtīkaraṇa*) should be performed for substances of excellent quality; thus the ash becomes indestructible and bestows longevity and health. (Āk 1.7.174)
(The Sequence of Service for the Essence of Abhraka): Now I shall explain the service regarding the elixir of the essence of *ghanasattva*.
One whose self is purified by emetics and other purifications, and who has worshipped his chosen deity, [should proceed]. (Āk 1.7.175)
One should lick a dose of one *guñjā* of mercury-satva and two *niṣkas* of powdered *triphalā* with honey and ghee in the morning; thus one should practice this for one month. (Āk 1.7.176)

In this manner, O Goddess, by increasing the dose month by month until the end of sixteen months, there shall be an increase in the *guñjā* weight; thus one should practice this elixir (*rasāyana*). (Āk 1.7.177)
O Goddess of the Gods, one should perform the ritual as previously described, even while avoiding [forbidden] acts;
by one year the purification of the body occurs, and after two years one is freed from disease. (Āk 1.7.178)
For three years, it will certainly destroy great diseases;
for four years, it increases great beauty, strength, and vigor. (Āk 1.7.179)
Within five years there is firmness of the body; indeed, in the sixth year one attains perfection of speech;
in the seventh there shall be divine vision; and in the eighth, the destruction of poison. (Āk 1.7.180)
In the ninth year, one attains perfection; thereafter, one becomes a Vidyādhara.
In the eleventh year, however, one attains the status of Indra, and in the twelfth, the state of Brahmā. (Āk 1.7.181)
In the thirteenth year he attains the state of Viṣṇu, in the fourteenth the state of Rudra, in the fifteenth the state of Īśa, and in the sixteenth year he becomes Sadāśiva. (Āk 1.7.182)
Endowed with the powers such as *aṇimā*, he becomes independent, all-knowing, and the doer of all. (The liquefaction of mica):
Now I shall describe the liquefaction of mica (*abhrakadruti*) and also the bulbous root of *kañcukī*. Āk 1.7.183.
One should cast *kapitindu* and hair-oil (*keśataila*) three times each into a crucible and melt them; thereby, the liquefaction of the essence of mica (*abhra-sattva*) occurs. (Āk 1.7.184)
One should diligently reduce it to ash, like the essence of mica (*abhraka-sattva*).
(The qualities of mica:
It possesses the six tastes, destroys all diseases, and is the supreme pacifier of the three *doṣas*. (Āk 1.7.185)
It increases vigor, lifespan, strength, wisdom, loveliness, and physical form; it bestows firmness and stability upon the body, and destroys wrinkles, graying hair, and death. (Āk 1.7.186)
Abhraka (mica) is pleasing, aphrodisiac, light, cooling, intellect-promoting, unctuous, and a rejuvenative; it is digestive, constipating, and the best for binding mercury. (Āk 1.7.187)

The mineral essence (*satva*) of mica, reduced to ash by the king of elixirs (*sūtarāja*) that conquers the wings [of mercury], destroys disease when in the form of mica-leaf (*patra*), and that same essence makes the body firm. (Āk 1.7.188)
Gentleness removes the state of being a sentient being; and speed removes both that and poverty.
Āk, 1, 8 (The Practice of Rasāyana):
Mercury, diamond, gold, kāntaloha, and likewise mica;
These five nectars have been conceived by me for the sake of human beings. (Āk 1.8.1)
He who knows the *mattakāśinī* is himself Maheśvara manifest;
I am the essence (*rasa*) and the essence is I—there is indeed no difference between us. (Āk 1.8.2)
When joined with that, the Vajra and other [mantras] will undoubtedly bestow accomplishment;
listen, O Pārvatī, as I describe the person worthy of practicing with mercury (rasa). Āk 1.8.3.

The elixir should certainly not be administered to women, eunuchs, or children; those under fifteen years of age are considered children, and those up to thirty years of age are considered youths. (Āk 1.8.4)
Those approximately fifty years of age are proclaimed as "youths";
beyond that, they would be considered "elders" in the context of *rasāyana*.
As it has been stated, success through the elixir for a youth shall occur within that time;
therefore, for a young man, success will certainly be achieved in twice that time. (Āk 1.8.6)
Therefore, having increased [the practice] by three times the duration of the *guṇas*, one shall attain success;
for, O Goddess, the superior, middling, and inferior [levels] are to be known in their proper sequence. (Āk 1.8.7)
(The Procedure for the Practice of Rasāyana):
First one should consume mica (*abhraka*), then the *rasāyana* of magnetite (*kānta*); then, O Goddess, the *rasāyana* of both magnetite and mica, and finally the *rasāyana* of gold. (Āk 1.8.8)
Then there is the elixir of mica combined with gold, the elixir of iron and gold,
the elixir of mica, iron, and gold, and thereafter the elixir of diamond.
Then follows the service of cloud-diamond and magnet-diamond;
thereafter, dense-iron-magnet-diamond and gold-diamond shall arise. (Āk 1.8.10)
Subsequently, there is the vajra of cloud-gold, the vajra of magnetite and gold, the dense magnetite-vajra, and the gold-vajra; thereafter follows the consumption of mercury. Āk 1.8.11.
Likewise, there would be the application of the essence of mica; from that, the essence of magnetite (kānta) arises.
O Goddess, after the essence of magnetite, the essence of gold arises. (Āk 1.8.12)
First there is the essence of *ghana* gold, then the essence of lovely gold;
from that comes *ghanakānta* and the gold-essence, and thereafter the essence of *vajra* shall arise. (Āk 1.8.13)
O Goddess, [there are] the essence of dense vajra, then the essence of lovely vajra;
then dense-lovely vajra-mercury, and then gold-vajra-essence. (Āk 1.8.14)
There is indeed nothing superior to this: the essence of solid gold and diamonds, which possesses the brilliance of lovely golden armor and the strength of beautiful golden heroes. Āk 1.8.15.
O fair-faced one, all these five elixirs (rasāyana) are progressively superior in their qualities, each one being better than the last. Āk 1.8.16.

There are two tastes produced from two medicinal substances each, ten produced from three medicinal substances each, five produced from four medicinal substances each, and one produced from five medicinal substances. (Āk 1.8.17)
O lady of excellent hips, O beloved, the elixir consists of thirty-one ingredients: iron, magnetite, gold, diamond, mercury, and the rest. (Āk 1.8.18)
O beloved of Prāṇa, there arise successive qualities of excellence;
the transmutation of mercury results in a diamond, gold, and dense [metal]. (Āk 1.8.19)

O Dear One, the transmutation of iron becomes gold, and that which is lovely becomes the void; one should employ the transmutation of gold produced from iron, and the transmutation of iron by means of mercury. Āk 1.8.20.
The transmutation of mica and the essence of mica grant accomplishment;
therefore, the aforementioned transmutation occurs through the employment of each individual medicinal herb. (Āk 1.8.21)
One should employ two, three, four, or five medicinal ingredients; however, there is no fixed rule for the process of inducing movement (*krāmaṇa*).
Triphalā, honey, and ghee constitute the general method for inducing movement. (Āk 1.8.22)
Āk, 1, 9 (The processing of juice suitable for elixirs;
first method)
Śrī Bhairavī:
O Lord, tell me the purification of mercury (sūta) that is fit for alchemy (rasāyana).
Śrī Bhairava:
Listen attentively, O Pārvatī, to the purification and other rites of consecration. Āk 1.9.1.

O Goddess, one should grind equal parts of *dhānyābhra* and mercury with the juice of *punarnavā* for one day in a heated mortar (*taptakhalva*), having placed the mercury inside a *vajramūṣā* crucible.
And once again, one should crush it in the mountain-press;
then, as before, there is further maceration and cooking with the previous liquids. (Āk 1.9.3)
Having performed this ten times, O Goddess, that mercury (pārada) should be cast into the dropping apparatus; thus purified, it is fit to be employed in alchemical elixirs (rasāyana). (Āk 1.9.4)
(Second Method) One should place the fragrance, which is one-tenth part of the mercury, into a heated mortar;
one should then grind it for one watch (yāma) with the juices of varā, jambīra, kanyā, and agni. Āk 1.9.5.
One should cause it to fall in a *pātanāyantra* in this manner seven times; O Dear One, by means of grinding with sulphur (*gandhaka*), the process of falling (*pātana*) occurs. (Āk 1.9.6)
O Goddess, mercury becomes pure and fit for yoga and alchemy.
(The third method: It should be rubbed with sesame oil, buffalo urine, and sour gruel. ĀK 1.9.7.
One should cook cinnabar with beef in an iron vessel over a gradual fire for seven days, constantly stirring the liquid mixture with an iron rod. (Āk 1.9.8)
One should saturate cinnabar with fresh peacock bile in the sun for a day, and then cook it in a *pātanāyantra* over a fierce fire. (Āk 1.9.9)
Mercury becomes pure after four stages of processing and is fit for alchemical elixirs (*rasāyana*).
(The process of mercury calcination;
first method.)
Equal parts of sulfur should be added to the mercury that has been processed [by heating] from above and below.
One should place [the substance] four times the amount [of the other ingredients] into a crucible in a pit;
having added the juice of *kākamācī*, one should seal it and heat it with a gradual fire. (Āk 1.9.11)

Having placed the crucible containing the mercury inside a *pacedguṇḍaka* furnace for four *yāmas*, the mercury is reduced to ashes; one should then employ it in alchemical elixirs (*rasāyana*). (Āk 1.9.12)

(Second method: One should grind old mercury together with equal parts of sulphur and the milky sap of *Euphorbia neriifolia* for one day; then, using a crucible with an inner chamber (*garbhayantra*), one should roast it in a fire-pit (*puṭa*) as previously described until it becomes ash. Āk 1.9.13.
(Third Method) One should grind together for one day equal parts of digested mercury, lac, wool-fiber, honey, borax, and *guñjā*, using the juice of *bhṛṅga*. Āk 1.9.14.
Having covered it with a seal, one should heat the mercury in a crucible made of diamond until it becomes ash.
(The fourth method.
One should grind together for three days equal parts of mercury that has been fully digested by *ghana* and sulphur. Āk 1.9.15.
Or with the juice of *ahimārī*, or with the juice of *ajā-mārī*, or with the juice of *kīṭamāriṇī*, or with the juice of white *aṅkola*. (Āk 1.9.16)
Day and night, one should burn [the mercury] in a clay crucible over a fire of dried cow-dung or a fire of husks;
after three days, the mercury is reduced to ashes. (Āk 1.9.17)

When the mercury has been digested for three days with an equal amount of vajra-ash in a heated mortar, it should be rubbed with the juices of haṃsapādī and with seeds produced from divine medicinal plants. Āk 1.9.18.
One should coat [the vessel] in a vajra-mūṣā crucible; first, one should place the mercury there.
It should then be cooked for three days over a fire of chaff, and again with the juices of haṃsapādī. (Āk 1.9.19)
One should grind it firmly for three days and cook that ball as before;
the lord of mercury becomes a powder resembling a conch shell, a jasmine flower, or the moon. (Āk 1.9.20)
(The Killing of the Digested Mercury;
the First Method) Now, O Goddess of the Gods, I shall explain the killing of mercury once it has been digested.
O Goddess, one should first perform the digestion (jāraṇa) with the seed-syllable (sabīja). Āk 1.9.21.
If a fool, through negligence, should cause the undigested *rasa* to be expelled as stool, he is my betrayer;
that most sinful man shall be guilty of a great transgression (*mahāpātaka*). (Ākāśabhairava-tantra 1.9.22)

The killer of a fetus, the murderer of a guru, the slayer of a cow, and the killer of women or children—therefore, with every effort, one should perform [the rite] preceded by the process of *jāraṇa*. (Āk 1.9.23)
O Pārvatī, the killing of the king of essences, which is my seed-syllable, is performed by placing cow dung upon the earth, O Goddess, and then [placing it] on top of that. Āk 1.9.24.
Having placed [the vessel] in a fired crucible and having poured oil derived from bitter gourd (*kaṭutumbī*) into its midst, one should then place the mercury on top of it. (Āk 1.9.25)
O fair-faced one, the juice of *kākamācī* equal in measure to the oil should be added;
having placed a pure fragrant substance the size of a grain of rice, one should seal the crucible. (Āk 1.9.26)
Above that, one should place a vessel filled with charcoal from the *khadira* tree;
once it is known that the vessel has cooled to the temperature of one's own body, one should again apply fragrant oil. (Āk 1.9.27)
Having added the juice of *kākamācī*, one should thus repeatedly apply fire;
there should be thick cow-dung below and fire above. (Āk 1.9.28)
Equal parts of the juice of *kākamācī*, mercury, and oil—these three combined—are used to digest six times the amount of sulfur; in this manner, the mouth [of the mercury] is prepared. (Āk 1.9.29)
One should then grind that mercury for a day with the juice of *jambīra* fruit;
[one should apply] a leaf of gold weighing sixty-four parts, which has been pierced by thorns. (Āk 1.9.30)
One should smear it with peacock bile and mustard oil;
in the absence of oil and bile, one should offer a bali-oblation of *cūlikā* salt. Āk 1.9.31.
Having ground that mercury with the juices of *jambīra*, one should cook the gold leaf in fire as before, again with the juices of *jambīra*. (Āk 1.9.32)
One should seal the crucible completely and digest [the substance] again as before;
then, thirty-two parts of gold [are added], and above that, sixteen parts. (Āk 1.9.33)
In this manner, one should rub and dissolve it; thereafter follows the killing of the mercury (sūta).
Taking a kumbhī plant together with its roots, one should grind it with cow urine. (Āk 1.9.34)
The wise one should grind mercury with that juice for one day, having placed it in a crucible made of magnetite (kāntaloha), with restraining agents (niyāmaka) both above and below. (Āk 1.9.35)
It should be cooked in a small vessel over a mild fire for one day until it becomes ash;
this mercury, when not diminished, shall be a destroyer of death, and a remover of old age and poverty. (Āk 1.9.36)
(Second Method) One *karṣa* of perfumed mercury, eight *guñjās* of gold,
and four *guñjās* of dead diamond should be ground with the juices of *haṃsapādī*. (Āk 1.9.37)
Having placed [the mercury] in a *vajramūṣā* crucible within a heated mortar, one should seal it; then, having taken that mercury again, one should cook it in a *bhūdharayantra*. ĀK 1.9.38.
One should grind [the mercury] with the juices of *haṃsapādī* in a heated mortar for three days;
then, one should cook the mercury repeatedly in the *bhūdhara* apparatus as before. (ĀK 1.9.39)
Having processed it in this way through one hundred layers, the ash shall be red in color;
these mercurial ashes are recommended for the practice of *rasāyana*.
(Alchemical Formulas for Elixirs; Iron-based Elixir): An elixir prepared with one, two, three, four, or five combinations [of ingredients].
O Goddess of the gods, I shall explain in due order the practice of consuming abhraka there as well. (Āk 1.9.41)

One whose self has been purified by emetics and other therapies, and who has abandoned alkaline, sour, and similar substances, should—as before—incinerate the essence of the *ākāśa* element with the juices of the best *bhṛṅgarāja*. (Āk 1.9.42)
One should cultivate this for twenty-one days; in the morning, one should take two guñjā seeds with sugar, and thereafter lick honey and ghee mixed with the three myrobalans (triphalā). Āk 1.9.43.
An increase of thirty-two guñjās and a dose of one karṣa for the transmutation [of mercury]—at the end of sixteen months, one is liberated from all diseases. (Āk 1.9.44)
By thus using mica (*abhraka*), one becomes worthy of using magnetite (*kānta*); [this is] the *kānta-rasāyana*.
One should reduce the magnetite to ash as before, using the juices of *varā*, *nirguṇḍī*, and *bhṛṅga*. (Āk 1.9.45)
One should grind [the medicine] with juices for twenty-one days and saturate it in sequence;
one should regularly lick it every morning, measuring two *guñjā* seeds, along with honey and clarified butter. (Āk 1.9.46)

Having purified one's body through emetics and other means, one should consume a karṣa measure of the pollen from the flowers of the excellent sinduvāra and bhṛṅga, mixed with honey and clarified butter, as a supplementary food. (Āk 1.9.47)
O Goddess, an increase of thirty-two guñjās is the maximum limit; by the end of sixteen months, one becomes free from old age and disease. (Āk 1.9.48)
By serving *kāntaloha*, one subsequently becomes worthy of *kāntābhraka* (the elixir of magnetite and mica).
[This is] the *kāntābhrarasāyana*.
Equal parts of dead *kāntaloha*, mica (*ghana*), *dhātrī*, *bhṛṅga*, and *punarnavā* [should be used]. (Āk 1.9.49)

Having ground these separately with their respective liquids, one who has been purified by emetics and other therapies should lick two *guñjā* seeds at dawn, along with sugar, honey, and clarified butter. (Āk 1.9.50)
The powder of *bhṛṅga*, *āmalaka*, and *varṣābhū* is an excellent *krāmaṇa*;
it should be licked after with honey and clarified butter, increasing the dose up to thirty-two *guñjās*. (Āk 1.9.51)

By practicing this yoga for sixteen months, one becomes strong, overcoming wrinkles and graying hair; through devotion to the essence of the lovely cloud, one becomes worthy of serving gold. (Āk 1.9.52)
(The Gold Elixir):
As before, one should reduce gold to ash with a decoction of the ten roots (*daśamūla*).
O Dear One, one should then grind and saturate that [ash] twenty-one times. (Āk 1.9.53)
Having purified his intellect, the wise man should lick a measure of mung beans mixed with honey and clarified butter in the morning;
thereafter, he should drink one *pala* of a decoction of *guḍūcī* and *triphalā*. (Āk 1.9.54)
The increase may continue up to eight guñjās over sixteen months;
[the practitioner] becomes radiant, strong, wise, possessed of keen vision, and free from disease. (Āk 1.9.55)
One becomes free from wrinkles and graying hair and a conqueror of the poisons of the three times.
(The Elixir of Gold and Abhraka): One should kill the gold as before, and [add] twice that amount of abhraka. Āk 1.9.56.
It should be processed twenty-one times with decoctions of the ten roots, varā, and bhṛṅgī;
three māṣas should be licked every morning, and one should lick the *krāmaṇa* with honey and ghee. (Āk 1.9.57)
O Pārvatī, thereafter one should drink a *pala* of the decoction of *guḍūcī* and *triphalā*;
the dose for this [mercury] should increase by twenty-four *guñjās*, with that being the maximum limit. (Āk 1.9.58)
Through the application of sixteen months, he becomes possessed of divine splendor and great strength;
through the application of solid gold, he becomes worthy of a golden complexion. (Āk 1.9.59)
(The Alchemy of Gold and Iron):
One should kill gold and iron as previously described, using two parts of iron for every part of gold;
one should then saturate and grind them sequentially with the fruits of the *dhātrī* tree twenty-one times. (Āk 1.9.60)
O Goddess of the Gods, one should consume three *māṣas* of this with sugar in the morning and afterwards drink a *karṣa* each of the essence of *dhātrī*, clarified butter, and honey. (Āk 1.9.61)
An increase of twenty-four *guñjās* shall be the maximum limit;
by practicing this for sixteen months, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Possessing the luster of molten gold like a second five-arrowed god of love, he was worthy of beautiful women and fine gold through his enjoyment of lovely maidens. (Āk 1.9.63)

(The Alchemy of Gold, Iron, and Abhraka) One should kill gold, the essence of iron (*kāntasattva*), and the essence of mica (*abhrasattva*) as previously described; these three, taken in equal parts, should then be processed twenty-one times [with the appropriate juices]. (Āk 1.9.64)
O Pārvatī, one should lick three māṣas of muṇḍī, nirguṇḍī, bhṛṅgarāja, and varānīra in the morning, mixed with honey and ghee. (Āk 1.9.65)
O Pārvatī, one should subsequently lick one karṣa of powdered Muṇḍī with honey and clarified butter, and then drink one pala of cow’s milk. Āk 1.9.66.
O Dear One, when the supreme increase numbered twelve *vallās* occurs, a man shall possess a divine body through the conjunction of sixteen months. (Āk 1.9.67)
By consuming gold and mica, one becomes fit for the consumption of *vajra* (the diamond-elixir).
(*Vajrarasāyana*) One should reduce the *vajra* to ash as before and grind it with the juice of *dhātrī*. (Āk 1.9.68)
The wise one should meditate upon it sevenfold and lick it, O Dear One, when it has reached the size of a grain of rice;
then he should drink a pala of emblic myrobalan juice mixed with ghee and honey. (Āk 1.9.69)
Through the application for sixteen months, the increase shall reach the limit of *vallā*;
one becomes long-lived, possessed of a vajra-body, divine vision, and great strength. (Āk 1.9.70)
By the practice of *vajra*, one becomes fit for consuming *vajrābhra* (the elixir of diamond-cloud).
(The Elixir of Diamond-Cloud) One should kill the sky (*vyoma*) as before, using a *vajra* four times the quantity of the *vajrābhra*. Āk 1.9.71.

The powder of *dhātrī* should be saturated seventy-three times with the juices of *śatāvarī*. One should lick a portion the size of a barley grain in the morning, followed by honey and clarified butter. (Āk 1.9.72)
One pala of the juice of *dhātrī* and *śatāvarī* is the dose for the initial administration;
thereafter, the increase shall be four *guñjās* every sixteen months. (Āk 1.9.73)
Through the service of Ghanavajra, one attains mastery of speech, divine vision, and a radiance equal to that of a deity; one becomes worthy of the beautiful Vajra. (Āk 1.9.74)
(The Alchemical Elixir of Kānta-Vajra): One should reduce vajra to ash as previously described; kānta iron is four times the amount of the vajra.
The kānta iron should be processed twenty-one times with the juices of aśvagandhā and varā. (Āk 1.9.75)
At the break of day, one should lick a dose the size of a barley grain mixed with honey and clarified butter;
one should drink one *karṣa* of the powder of *aśvagandhā* and *varā* with cow's milk. (Āk 1.9.76)
The increase should be known to extend up to the limit of four *guñjās*;
through the application of sixteen months, [the mercury] attains a radiance equal to the rising sun. (Āk 1.9.77)

Possessing great strength and great splendor, one who has mastered speech shall attain perfection through service to the beloved of Vajra; such a person is worthy of the beloved of Vajra and of the *abhraka* stone. Āk 1.9.78.
(Vajrābhrakarasāyana):

One should kill the vajra, kānta-iron, and mica using diamond as before; [this is done] with four times the amount of kānta-iron and mica, along with the juices of varā, bhṛṅga, and kuraṇḍaka. (Āk 1.9.79)
O beloved, it should be processed with juices twenty-one times;
one should lick it in the measure of a barley grain, combined with honey, clarified butter, the juice of *bhṛṅgarāja*, and the pollen of *karuṇḍaka*. (Āk 1.9.80)
One should drink cow’s milk starting from one *pala* up to a maximum of four *guñjās*;
by practicing this for sixteen months, one attains the vision of a vulture and great strength. (Āk 1.9.81)
The steadfast one, whose movement is unimpeded, moves together with the host of Siddhas;
he becomes worthy of lovely clouds, vajras, and vessels, as well as of gold and diamonds. (Āk 1.9.82)
(The Alchemy of Gold and Vajra):
One should process the vajra as before; gold in two parts [relative to] the vajra [should be processed].
The gold-vajra compound should be infused twenty-one times with the juice of *Varṣābhū*. (Āk 1.9.83)
O Goddess of the Suras, one should lick *punarnavā* measured by a *vrīhi* grain with honey and ghee; thereafter, one should drink a *karṣa* or a *pala* of cow’s milk as an after-drink. (Āk 1.9.84)
By increasing [the dose] by two *guñjās* over the course of sixteen months, one shall live for a long time, free from wrinkles and grey hair. (Āk 1.9.85)
By means of the application of vajra and gold, one becomes worthy of the elixir of golden cloud-vajra (*svarṇābhra-kuliśa*).
O Pārvatī, as before, one should reduce to ash the gold, the clouds, and the vajras. (The Golden Cloud-Vajra Elixir). *Ākṣepapañcāśikā* 1.9.86.
Gold is twice the weight of the diamond, and abhra is two parts relative to the gold; it should be infused twenty-one times with the essence of the musalī tuber. (Āk 1.9.87)
One should lick a measure of barley-sized powder in the morning with honey and clarified butter, and afterwards drink one karṣa of *musalī* powder with one pala of cow’s milk. (Āk 1.9.88)
By increasing [the dose] up to four guñjās through the application of sixteen months, one conquers death, becomes free from old age, possesses a vajra-body, and attains great strength. (Āk 1.9.89)
By the service of this [elixir], one becomes worthy of diamond, gold, and *kānta* iron; [this is] the elixir (*rasāyana*) of gold, diamond, and *kānta* iron.
Furthermore, diamond, *kānta*, and gold are to be killed as previously described. (Āk 1.9.90)
Gold is twice the amount of the vajra, and kānta iron is two parts relative to the gold;
this should be ground with the juices of dhātrī and bhṛṅga twenty-one times. (Āk 1.9.91)

In the morning, one should lick a barley-measure of the powder made from *dhātrī* and *bhṛṅga*, followed by drinking one *karṣa* with honey and clarified butter, along with one *pala* of cow's milk. (Āk 1.9.92)
Through the application of sixteen months, there is an increase of four *guñjās*;
freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one becomes possessed of divine luster and great strength. (Āk 1.9.93)
By means of its service, one who is worthy of gold, cinnabar, diamond, and mica should reduce gold, cinnabar, mica,
and diamonds to ash according to the prescribed method. (The Elixir of Gold, Cinnabar, Diamond, and Mica) Āk 1.9.94.

One should saturate [the powder] twenty-one times with the juices of *jyotiṣmatī*; one should lick a portion the size of a barley grain every morning, followed by drinking honey and clarified butter. (Āk 1.9.95)
One *karṣa* of powdered *aśvagandhā* root, one *pala* of cow’s milk, and an increase of four *guñjās* at a time—this, O Goddess, is the maximum limit. (Āk 1.9.96)
Through the practice for sixteen months, one becomes directly equal to Indra;
O Goddess, by means of this service, one is worthy to consume the mercury. (Āk 1.9.97)

One should grind paddy-processed mica (dhānyābhra) and mercury in a heated mortar for three days with the juices of triphalā, āragvadha, niśā, kumārī, and kṛṣṇadhūrta. (This is the preparation of rasabhasma.)
One should rub [the substance] with the juices of punarnavā, agni, and jambīra, and then cause it to fall in a *pātanāyantra*;
thus is the process of rubbing and causing to fall.
One should process it three times; thus the mercury becomes pure and free from defects.
One should grind it with fixatives and apply those same fixatives as a coating to the crucible.
Having ground that mercury and placed it in a crucible, the wise one, having sealed it, should cook it in the apparatus called *bhūdhara*, O Goddess of the Suras. (Āk 1.9.101)
In this manner, one should perform the mardana and puṭapācana seven times;
thus the mercury ash (rasabhasma) becomes pure and may be employed in alchemical elixirs (rasāyana). Āk 1.9.102.
(The juices of *āroṭaka*;
the ash of mercury processed with mica):
Now, the juice of *āroṭaka* is the sole cause for the perfection of the body.
One should lick a measure of one māṣa in the morning together with honey, clarified butter, and triphalā. (Āk 1.9.103)
O beloved, cow’s milk that remains warm after being drawn should be drunk in measured doses;
increasing the amount by eight *guñjā*s at a time until it reaches sixteen *māṣakas*. (Āk 1.9.104)
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one shall live as long as the moon and stars;
O Goddess, by the service of this [mercury], one indeed becomes worthy of the extraction of mica-ore. (Āk 1.9.105)
O Goddess, when the mercury has been made into a mouthful weighing sixty-four *niṣkas*, one should add one *niṣka* of iron ore (*abhrasattva*) along with the juices of *jambīra* fruits. (Āk 1.9.106)
One should grind it for one day in a heated mortar using a kacchapayantra;
then, having added viḍa salt, one should cook it and subsequently take it up and grind it again. (Āk 1.9.107)
O Pārvatī, two niṣkas of mineral essence (abhrasattva) should be processed with the acidic juice of jambīra in a heated mortar using the apparatus known as the kacchapa. Āk 1.9.108.
In the third [falling], one should give four niṣkas; in the fourth and fifth, respectively, eight niṣkas and a being made of iron (abhrasatva) should be given during the fifth falling. (Āk 1.9.109)
In the sixth [day], there is sixteen niṣkas of mercury and a thirty-second part;
in the seventh, O Pārvatī, there is sattva, exactly the same amount. Āk 1.9.110.
O Dear One, the digestion of the essence of mica occurs in mercury;
once the lord of mercury has been thus digested, one should reduce it to ash as previously described. (Āk 1.9.111)
One *pala* of this mercury ash and four *palas* of the essence of *vyoma* (mica) should be rubbed with the juice of *bhṛṅgarāja* and firmly sealed within a crucible.

One should cook it in a crucible called *kukkuṭa* and collect it when it has cooled to the temperature of one's own body; one should then saturate it twenty-one times with water derived from *triphalā* and *bhṛṅgarāja*. (Āk 1.9.113)

One of purified intellect, with a restrained mind, should lick a dose the size of a *guñjā* seed of honey and clarified butter in the morning, and afterwards drink a *pala* of the decoction of *varā*. (Āk 1.9.114)
The increase is sixteen *guñjās*; it should be consumed for sixteen months.
One shall live as long as the moon and stars, free from wrinkles and grey hair. (Āk 1.9.115)
By the service of this [mercury], one becomes worthy of serving the beloved king of mercury (*sūtarāja*);
once the king of mercury has been made into a mouth [of the vessel], the digestion of mica (*abhrajāraṇā*) occurs as it did before. (The ash of the digested mercury of the beloved). *Āk* 1.9.116.
In the same way, O Dear One, there is the digestion (*jāraṇā*) of *kānta* metal by means of *satva*;
one should kill the mercury (*sūta*) that has been digested by *kānta-satva* as previously described. (Āk 1.9.117)
In this manner, there shall again be one part consisting of ashes;
furthermore, one should grind four parts of *kāntaloha* ash with the decoction of *triphalā*. (Āk 1.9.118)
One should then close it in a crucible and subsequently cook it in a *kaukkuṭika* type of *puṭa*.
Having taken that out, one should saturate it with the juice of *varā* twenty-one times.

O Goddess of the Gods, one who is free from sloth should lick a dose the size of a *guñjā* seed with honey and clarified butter every morning, followed by a *pala* measure of cow's milk to drink. (Āk 1.9.120)
An increase of sixteen *guñjās* occurs through the conjunction with sixteen months;
one shall attain divine vision, the power of moving through the sky (*khecaratva*), and the state of Indra. (Āk 1.9.121)
By serving this [substance], one becomes worthy of the company of celestial nymphs;
when the mercury has been activated, one should perform the digestion (*jāraṇa*) of mica as before. (Āk 1.9.122)

O Goddess of Gods, the wise should subsequently perform [the processing] with an equal amount of the ash of mercury digested in magnetic iron (*kāntābhra*). As before, the digestion of the essence of magnetic iron should be done using an amount equal to the king of mercuries (*sūtarāja*). (Āk 1.9.123)
If mercury is processed with *kānta* iron and *abhrasattva*, that *rasa* becomes wingless, free from volatility, and auspicious. (ĀK 1.9.124)
That mercury, killed by divine medicinal herbs as previously described, [weighs] one *pala*; twice that amount is the ash of the essence of *vyoma*, and an equal amount of that [ash]. (Āk 1.9.125)
The ash of vaikrānta-sattva should likewise be rubbed three times with each of these three substances;
then, one should cook it in a small crucible using the juice of *bhṛṅga* and *dhātrī* fruits.
One should macerate the mercury in the juice of *bhṛṅga* and *dhātrī* fruits in the shade;
thereafter, one should lick a dose the size of a *guñjā* berry along with *triphalā*, honey, and clarified butter. (Āk 1.9.127)
One should drink one *pala* of cow's milk with an increase of sixteen *guñjās* [per day];
by practicing this for sixteen months, one may live as long as the moon and stars endure. (Āk 1.9.128)
By serving this, one becomes worthy of serving mercury and gold;
one should reduce mercury that has digested gold to ash, as previously described. (This refers to the ash of mercury that has digested gold. Āk 1.9.129.
One pala of such processed mercury-ash and two palas of gold should be infused three times with the juices of *bhṛṅga* and *dhātrī* fruits in the shade. (Āk 1.9.130)
Having enclosed it in a casket, one should cook it; one should cook it in a crucible known as *kukkuṭapuṭa*.
Then, one should saturate it twenty-one times with the juices of *bhṛṅgarāja* and *dhātrī*. (Āk 1.9.131)

In the morning, one should lick a dose of one *māṣa* of the juice combined with honey and clarified butter; cow’s milk should be drunk as an after-drink, and the dose should be increased by sixteen *māṣas*. (Āk 1.9.132)
Through the practice for sixteen months, one becomes equal to a god and long-lived;
by the service of the gold-elixir, one becomes worthy of the essence of refined gold.
First, the mineral essence of mica (*abhrasattva*) equal in amount [to the mercury] should be digested into the mercury that has been prepared as a mouth;
then gold equal in amount [to the mercury] should be digested; thereafter, one should reduce that mercury to ash. (Āk 1.9.134)
One should combine one *pala* of the previously mentioned sūta-bhasma, two *palas* of gold, and four *palas* of the bhasma of vyomasattva in a single place. (Āk 1.9.135)
O beloved, having ground it in the juice of indigo leaves for one day in a decoction of *varā*, one should seal it in a crucible and cook it with twenty other [fuel cakes of] cow dung. (Āk 1.9.136)
One should saturate it twenty-one times with the decoctions of the best indigo juice;
one should lick a dose the size of a *guñjā* berry at dawn, and afterwards drink honey and ghee. (Āk 1.9.137)
Taking one *pala* of the decoction of *varā* with an increase of sixteen *guñjās* per dose, through its use for sixteen months, one may live as long as the moon and stars endure. (Āk 1.9.138)
By the service of this [substance], one becomes worthy of digesting *kānta* and gold-based mercury (the ash of mercury digested with *kāntaloha*).
Into the face of the mercury (*pārada*), the essence of *kānta* should be digested according to the prescribed method. (Āk 1.9.139)

Likewise, one should digest gold with equal amounts of both; having thus digested it, one should reduce the mercury, which has been processed with *kāntaloha* and gold, to ash according to the prescribed method. (Āk 1.9.140)
One should duly combine one *pala* of that mercury, two *palas* of gold ash, and mobile iron-ore essence ash (*kāntasattva-bhasma*) according to the prescribed method. (Āk 1.9.141)
Having crushed the best of the *śatāvarī* roots in water for a day, one should seal it in a *saṃpuṭa* vessel and cook it in a *kukkuṭapuṭa*; then, having extracted that liquid— Āk 1.9.142.
It should be processed three times with sevenfold [portions] of the juices of *śatāvarī* and the juice of *varā*.
One should lick a dose the size of a *guñjā* seed combined with ghee and honey, and drink water afterwards. (ĀK 1.9.143)
O Goddess of the Suras, one *pala* of the juice of *śatāvarī* should be drunk;
by practicing this for sixteen months, there is an increase of sixteen *guñjās*. (Āk 1.9.144)
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, he lives until the end of the dissolution;
by the service of this [elixir], one becomes a consumer of the essence of gold, beauty, and clouds. Āk 1.9.145.

(Orpiment, mica, and the ash of digested mercury): O Dear One, one should gradually digest equal parts of thick, lustrous gold into the mercury that has been made into a mouth, O Beloved. (Āk 1.9.146)
The wise one should kill the mercury processed with mica and other minerals as previously described;
from that mercury reduced to ash, there should be twice the amount of gold ash. (Āk 1.9.147)
Dead iron equal in weight to mercury, and dead mercury equal in weight to iron—
this entire mixture should be processed for one day with the juices of varā, kvātha, muṇḍī, and bhṛṅga.

Having crushed it and sealed it within a *saṃpuṭa*, one should cook it in a *kaukkuṭika* fire-pit; then, having taken that [substance], one should saturate it with the juices of the excellent *bhṛṅga* and *muṇḍinī*. (Āk 1.9.149)

One should lick three times seven times in the shade a dose of *guñjā* the size of a jujube fruit in the morning; cow’s milk should be drunk afterwards, along with sugar, honey, and clarified butter. (Āk 1.9.150)
Through the practice of sixteen months, there is an increase of sixteen *guñjās*;
freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one shall live as long as the moon and stars endure. (Āk 1.9.151)
By the service of this, one becomes worthy of serving the vajra-mercury (*vajrasevārhaka*).
One should perform the digestion of the vajra in the presence of mercury (*pārada*), as before, using the ash of mercury that has been digested by the vajra (*vajrajīrṇarasabhasma*). (Āk 1.9.152)
O Goddess, one should reduce the diamond-weathered mercury to ash as before;
O Beloved, the diamond ash should be twice the amount of the reduced mercury. (Āk 1.9.153)

Having ground it for a day with the juices of *kanyā*, *bhṛṅga*, *varā*, and *anīra* in a *saṃpuṭa* vessel, one should cook it in a *puṭa* called *kukkuṭa*; then, taking that [substance], one should macerate it. (Āk 1.9.154)
One should saturate [the powder] twenty-one times with the juices of kanyā, bhṛṅga, vara, and anīra;
one should lick a portion the size of a barley grain every morning and drink honey and ghee afterwards. (Āk 1.9.155)
Taking one pala of cow's milk with an increase of four guñjās [per day], through the practice for sixteen months, one may live as long as the moon and stars. (Āk 1.9.156)
By the service of this, one becomes worthy of the adamantine thread and the sky.
The wise person should reduce to ash the mercury that has been digested by mica and the mercury that has been digested by adamant. Āk 1.9.157.
From the reduced-to-ashes mercury, take double the amount of vajra and four times as much of sky-ash; having combined all of these together, one should grind them thoroughly. Āk 1.9.158.

One should cook it for a day in a sealed crucible with the juices of varā in a decoction of varā; after performing a light puṭapāka, it should subsequently be processed with the juices of bhṛṅga and varā. (Āk 1.9.159)
One should drink honey and clarified butter, mixed in three parts and seven parts respectively, followed by a dose the size of a black gram (māṣa).
Cow’s milk, one pala in measure, should be drunk; the increase [of the dose] continues until it reaches eight guñjās. (Āk 1.9.160)
Thus, by living for sixteen months, one may live as long as the moon and stars;
through this service, one becomes worthy of the lineage of Kāntavajra. (Āk 1.9.161)
(Regarding the ash of mercury digested by magnetite and diamond):
O beloved, magnetite and diamond should be digested together in the presence of mercury. Once that mercury has been digested by magnetite and diamond, the wise practitioner should fix it. Āk 1.9.162.
According to the previously mentioned procedure, one should take this mercury ash along with the magnetite;
the diamond should be twice the amount of the mercury, and the magnetite four times the amount of the diamond. (Āk 1.9.163)
Having ground it for a day with the fresh juices of *palāśa* flowers, one should seal it in a *saṃpuṭa* vessel;
then, having placed it inside a *kukkuṭaka* crucible, one should subsequently take it up and perform the impregnation (*bhāvanā*). (Āk 1.9.164)
One should saturate it twenty-one times with the juice of *palāśa* flowers;
then, having mixed it with honey and clarified butter, one should lick a portion the size of a black gram (*māṣa*) and afterwards drink milk. (Āk 1.9.165)
The increase [of the dose] may continue up to eight *guñjā*s over sixteen months;
freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one shall live as long as the moon and stars. (Āk 1.9.166)
By the service of this [elixir], one becomes a master of mercury, mica, magnetite, and iron;
and into the mercury present before one, mica, magnetite, and vajra are added in succession. (The ash of mercury digested by magnetite, vajra, and mica. Āk 1.9.167.
Thereafter, one should digest equal amounts [of the minerals]; once that mercury is digested, one should kill it.
As before, from the mercury, one should take an equal amount of *vajra*, or four times the amount of *vajra*. (Āk 1.9.168)
One should grind these—kānta, kāntasama, and vyomasattva—with the juices of triphalā and bhṛṅgarāja, enclose them in a sealed crucible (saṃpuṭaka), and heat them. Āk 1.9.169.
Then, having taken that very substance with a small fire-capsule, one should process it twenty-one times in the heat with the juices of the excellent *Bhṛṅgarāja*. Āk 1.9.170.
One of purified intellect should lick a dose of one *māṣa* of this, mixed with honey and clarified butter, in the morning;
cow’s milk should be drunk afterwards, and the dosage should increase by eight *guñjās*. (Āk 1.9.171)
By practicing this for sixteen months, one may live as long as the moon and stars;
through its service, one becomes worthy of gold, vajra, and mercury. Āk 1.9.172.

Into mercury [already] processed with gold and diamond ash, one should digest equal amounts of gold and diamond; O Goddess, that mercury and the diamond should both be reduced to ash in equal proportions. (Āk 1.9.173)
One should grind equal parts of mercury and gold with a decoction of *varā* (Crataeva religiosa);
having placed all of that inside a crucible, one should cook it in a *bhūdhara*-named furnace. (Āk 1.9.174)
Having taken that, one should saturate it twenty-one times with decoctions of the best *vārāka* plant;
one should lick a dose of one *māṣa* in the morning, combined with sesame, clarified butter, and honey. (Āk 1.9.175)
Cow’s milk should not be drunk [after the ritual] up to eight *guñjās* in sequence;
until the end of sixteen months, one shall live as long as the moon and stars. (Āk 1.9.176)
By means of its service, mercury becomes capable of digesting space (vyoma), gold, and diamond;
one should digest space, gold, and diamond within the mercury that is present before one. (This refers to the ash of mercury that has digested gold, diamond, and mica. Āk 1.9.177.
Then, one should kill the mercury with equal parts of mercury; [add] dead diamond equal to the mercury, and gold equal to those two. Āk 1.9.178.
Having ground all those equal quantities of mercury and space (sulphur) together with the seeds of Brahma (musk) and oils for three days, one should seal it within a *bhūdhara* crucible.
One should perform twenty-one infusions of that [substance] with a decoction of *palāśa*;
then, one should take a *māṣa* measure of that liquid along with sesame oil and the seeds of *brahmadru*. (Āk 1.9.180)
One should drink a dose of one karṣa, increasing it until it reaches eight guñjās;
through this practice for sixteen months, one becomes perfected and eternal. (Āk 1.9.181)
By the service of this [substance], one becomes fit for the essence of *kānta*, gold, and diamond (i.e., the ash of the digested mercury of *kānta*, gold, and diamond).
When the king of alchemical elixirs (*sūtarāja*) has been processed, equal parts of *kānta* iron and gold [are added]. (Āk 1.9.182)
One should digest it and reduce it to ash; then, one should take an equal amount of that ash and of diamond-ash (*vajrabhasma*).
To these two, an equal amount of dead gold and *kānta* iron should be added, O beloved, with all [the other ingredients] being equal. (Āk 1.9.183)
Having ground [the substance] in the juice of *varā* and *bhṛṅga*, one should cook it in a crucible (*saṃpuṭa*) made of earth;
thereafter, one should perform twenty-one saturations with the water of *varā* and *bhṛṅga*.
The wise man should lick one *māṣa* measure of the juice with excellent honey in the morning;
one *pala* of cow’s milk should be drunk, and the dose should be increased by sixteen *māṣas*. (Āk 1.9.185)
Through the practice for sixteen months, one becomes a lord equal to a Siddha;
by the service of this [practice], one attains the essence of space, gold, and mercury.
That Maheśvara, whose self is restrained, becomes worthy of being served.
One should digest gold of intense luster and vajra within the mercury that has already digested mica, using the mercury in its "open mouth" state. Āk 1.9.187.
O Goddess of the Gods, each [of these] should be prepared in a quantity equal to mercury;
then, one should kill that purified iron by means of a skillful method until it is reduced to a state equal to mercury. Āk 1.9.188.
Mercury is equal to tin; mercury is equal to all [other metals]; iron is equal to steel; and steel is equal to the products of the celestial tree (sura-druja). Āk 1.9.189.
Then, having placed it inside a sealed vessel and smeared with oils, one should cook it in an earthen pot.
A pure and wise person should lick this mercury, in a dose of one *guñjā*, in the morning. (Āk 1.9.190)
O Pārvatī, one *karṣa* of oil extracted from *devadāru* should be drunk while it is still dripping hot, followed by one *pala* of cow's milk, O beloved. (Āk 1.9.191)
One who always eats wholesome food and consumes this divine mercury for sixteen months, increasing the dose up to sixteen *guñjās*, [attains the goal]. (Āk 1.9.192)
Free from disease, birth, old age, and death, possessing all supernatural powers, omniscient, omnipresent, and perfected, he creates as it were, like the Grandfather Brahmā. (Āk 1.9.193)
Like Viṣṇu, he protects the universe; like Hara himself, he removes [all evils];
and like another wish-fulfilling tree, he personally grants all desired objects. (Āk 1.9.194)
Like Kandarpa, he may delight a thousand Kāmākṣīs in an instant;
this one, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss, will certainly become a connoisseur of aesthetic rasa. (Āk 1.9.195)
This secret, difficult even for the gods to obtain, consisting of thirty-one elixirs arising from the five yogas beginning with *ghana*, has been told out of affection for you. (Āk 1.9.196)
Āk, 1, 10 (The Accomplishment of the Pill):
Having prostrated with supreme devotion to Bhairava, Bhairavī, and Śiva, [the author speaks].
Desiring the welfare of the worlds, she spoke this with humility.
Śrī Bhairavī said:
O God of gods, embodiment of compassion, Lord who bestows grace upon all!
By your favor, I have come to know this secret that is exceedingly difficult to attain. (Āk 1.10.2)
"O Mahādeva Bhairava, [I have heard] of the elixir consisting of the essence of mercury, mica, gold, and the ash of lightning; beyond this, I wish to hear more. (Āk 1.10.3)
Having heard these words of Bhairavī, which spoke of the elixir for those who have fashioned pills from these substances such as *ghana* and others, Ādibhairava [responded] with humility. (Āk 1.10.4)
Having stood [thus], Śrī Bhairava spoke these words: "I shall describe that elixir (rasāyana): (1. The Reviving Pill)."
Listen now with effort and with full attention, O Pārvatī. (Āk 1.10.5)
First, the process of digestion (jāraṇa) must be performed, followed by the binding of mercury.
Therefore, I shall describe to you the seeds for the digestion of iron and other metals. (Āk 1.10.6)
Sulphur, talaka, realgar, tuttha, kharparī, hiṅgula, amala, bhūnāga, tāpya, kāsīsa, nṛpāvarta, abhra, and gairika. Āk 1.10.7.
Kānta, the three alkalis (trikṣāra), and vaikrānta—these, taken in equal parts as a powder, are known as Siddhacūrṇa; it is excellent for the practice of seed-implantation (bījakarman). Āk 1.10.8.

O Dear One, one should place the essence of black mercury and the essence of mica, together with an equal amount of copper, into a crucible smeared with a mixture of the two [mercury and mica]. Āk 1.10.9.

In that [mixture], one should repeatedly add the *siddhacūrṇa*—ten times the amount of the *ghana*—along with the five ingredients including a friend; O fair-faced one, one should then blow it intensely. (Āk 1.10.10)
When only a solid essence remains, it should be sublimated for that duration;
by this time, this seed of the essence of space is to be matured in the practice of alchemy (*rasāyana*). (Āk 1.10.11)
One should add the seed (bīja) into the mercury (pārada) when it is in its pure state, at a proportion of one part in sixty-four;
then, in a heated mortar, one should grind it with the group of acids for three days. (Āk 1.10.12)
O beloved, one should digest that lead in a tortoise-shaped apparatus along with bitumen;
then, [one should add] thirty-two parts and sixteen parts of mercury. (Āk 1.10.13)
O Goddess of the Suras, one should thus digest the seed in mercury (pārada) in sequence: an eighth part, a fourth part, two parts, and an equal part. Āk_1,10.14.
O Dear One, one should grind this kind of Sūta, which is a celestial essence equal to the seed, in a heated mortar with the group of acidic substances for one day. Āk 1,10.15.
One should place that powder of the king of mercury inside a jambīra fruit and cook it for seven days in a dolāyantra (swinging apparatus) combined with acid. Āk 1,10.16.
Having taken that and cast it as an offering with the *siddha-cūrṇa*, O Pārvatī, one should then cook it in a *bhūdhara* yantra using the *laghu-puta* method. (Āk 1.10.17)

As long as it reaches a state of hardness, one should repeatedly perform the "swing-cooking" (dolāpāka), apply the "perfected powder" (siddhacūrṇa), and place it in a "mountain-oven" (bhūdharaka) seal. Āk_1,10.18 //
The pill named Mṛtasañjīvanī bestows all supernatural powers;
one should wear it in the mouth, on the throat, on the head, on the arm, or on the ear. (Āk 1.10.19)
When properly wrapped in gold, it completely destroys wrinkles and graying hair;
when worn on the face, it wards off death and, within a year, destroys poison and disease. (Āk 1.10.20)
One should drink one karṣa of pure fragrance and one pala of cow’s milk;
by this very sequence, the mercury enters the body. (Āk 1.10.21)

(2. Divine Pill) Having melted together equal amounts of magnetite and silver within a crucible smeared with a coating, one should slowly add a perfected powder ten times the amount of the magnetite. Āk_1,10.22.
One should repeatedly cause it to flow until only the "beloved" (kānta) remains;
this is declared to be the excellent "beloved seed" (kāntabīja), which is to be digested for the purpose of alchemical elixirs (rasāyana). (Āk 1.10.23)
When the mercury is in front, this seed and the *cārya* [substance] should be applied as before;
first in sixty-four parts, and then in equal portions, indeed in due order. (Āk 1.10.24)
One should grind this king of elixirs and the lovely seed— these two in equal parts— in a heated mortar with the group of acidic substances for three days.

Having reduced it to a paste, one should place it in a citron filled with a sour group of substances and cook it properly in a *dolāyantra* (swinging apparatus) in this manner for seven cycles. (Āk 1.10.26)
Taking that, O Bhairavī, one should lick it on the outside with the *siddhacūrṇa*;
then, having smeared the crucible with divine herbs, one should cook it in the earthen vessel. Āk 1.10.27.

One should proceed gradually until it reaches a state of hardness; then one should perform the "swinging" (dolāpāka), the application of the perfected powder (siddhacūrṇa), and the "earth-holding" cooking (bhūdharapācana). Āk 1.10.28.
O Supreme Goddess, one should cause those two to be digested within a crucible by means of the method called "divine";
then one should carry [the elixir] in the mouth, the throat, the head, the arm, or the ear. (Āk 1.10.29)
It should be worn well-wrapped with gold; it destroys wrinkles and graying hair.
Like the previous [amulets], this meritorious one bestows its fruit and should be worn with effort by men. (Āk 1.10.30)
The transference should be performed as before; the essence (rasa) migrates into the body. (3.
Kāmeśvarī Ghuṭikā) One should kill the seed of the sky-lustre (vyomakānta) within the mercury (pārada) facing it. Āk_1,10.31.
Each [substance] should be equal in measure to the mercury, and as before, very gradually;
first, one-sixty-fourth part, and then an equal portion, should be added to the mercury in due order. (Āk 1.10.32)
One should take equal parts of the seed of *kāntaloha* and *abhrabīja* (mica-seed) and grind them with the group of acidic substances (*amlavarga*) in a heated mortar for three days. (Āk 1.10.33)
Having ground it into a paste and placed it inside a citron, one should cook it in a swinging vessel (*dolāyantra*).
Then, taking that paste again, one should coat it with *siddhacūrṇa*. (Āk 1.10.34)
One should cook [the substance] in a crucible smeared with a collection of divine medicinal herbs; when it reaches a state of hardness, one should divide it into two parts in due order. Āk_1,10.35.
Having performed steaming in a swing, application of medicinal powder, and heating in an earthen vessel, this pill of Kāmeśvarī, when held in the mouth, bestows all accomplishments. (Āk 1.10.36)
As before, the transmutation (*krāmaṇa*) should be performed; the lord of mercury (*rasendra*) transmutes the body.
(4. The *ghuṭikā* of Hemasundarī:
Gold, silver, "barbarian-mouth" [copper], the essence of *kānta*, and the essence of mica. (Āk 1.10.37)
One should place that [substance] into a crucible smeared with a mixture of the two;
once it has melted therein, one should add the perfected powder (siddhacūrṇa), ten times the amount of gold. Āk_1,10.38 //
It should be slowly melted until only gold remains;
this is known as the seed of gold, the most excellent for the alchemical transformation of mercury. (Āk 1.10.39)
O Goddess, in the presence of mercury, one should gradually digest the seed [substance] equal in weight to the mercury, starting from sixty-four parts and so forth, as before, O Goddess. (Āk 1.10.40)
Having heated this mercury and gold seed in equal parts in a mortar, one should rub them with the group of acidic substances; after three days, the mercury will become a fine paste. (Āk 1.10.41)
O Goddess, having made a paste of *jambīra* [citron], one should cook it for six days in a *dolāyantra* filled with acid, while applying a coating of *siddhacūrṇa*. (Āk 1.10.42)
Likewise, one should perform the sealing with ointment and the baking on the earthen vessel, continuing as before until it reaches a state of hardness. Āk 1.10.43.
But this divine pill, renowned as Hemasundarī, bestows perfection upon those who place it in their mouths; it removes old age, death, and poison. (Āk 1.10.44)
As before, the transference should be performed; the mercury transmigrates once again.
When the mercury has been made receptive, the seed-syllable of space (*vyomabīja*) and the seed-syllable of gold (*hāṭakabījaka*) [are applied]. (5. Madanasundarī Ghuṭikā) Āk 1.10.45.
Having gradually processed equal amounts [of the two] in sixty-four parts and so forth, the mercury (sūta) thus processed becomes the seed (bīja) for both the sky (ākāśa) and gold. (Āk 1.10.46)

One should grind [the mercury] equal in weight to the *pārada* in a heated mortar (*taptakhalva*) with the group of acidic substances (*amlavarga*) for three days; thus a paste (*piṣṭi*) is produced, which one should then place in a *jambīra* fruit. (Āk 1.10.47)
One should cook it for seven days in a dolāyantra (swinging vessel) filled with acid; likewise, there is the application of *siddhacūrṇa* as a plaster and the sealing of the *saṃpuṭa*. Āk_1,10.48.
Likewise, when the digestion of the mountain [of mercury] reaches the state of hardness, this pill, known by the name Madanasundarī, bestows accomplishment. Āk 1.10.49.
Situated within the mouth, she bestows all accomplishments and long life;
she brings under control even serpents, tigers, elephants, kings, and women. (Āk 1.10.50)
As before, the transference should be performed; the mercury enters the body.
(6. Khecarī Ghuṭikā) When the mercury has been made into a mouth-paste, equal amounts of the seeds of iron and gold [should be added]. Āk_1,10.51.

Each of these should be digested separately [with mercury] in sixty-four parts and so forth; thus, when the mercury has been digested, one part each of the seed (bīja) and of black iron and gold, equal in measure to the garlic, [should be added]. Āk 1.10.52.
Having made a paste as before, one should cook it in a *dolāyantra* (swinging apparatus) repeatedly until it reaches a state of hardness. (Āk 1.10.53)
A pill arises by name Khecarī, which bestows all accomplishments;
the transference should be performed as before, and one should drink fragrant cow’s milk. (Āk 1.10.54)
By that [process], the mercury contained within the pill transmigrates into the body. (7.
Vajreśvarī Pill) When the mercury is in its proper state, it is mixed with equal parts of *vyomakānta* and gold. Āk_1,10.55.
The seed-syllables of ether and the other elements should be heated individually in portions of sixty-four parts and so forth;
for mercury thus prepared, the seed-syllables of ether and the rest are used in equal measure. (Āk 1.10.56)
One should rub that threefold [mixture] with *khalva* for three days using acid; that mercury attains the state of a paste (*piṣṭi*), and that paste, O beloved, [is treated] as before. (Āk 1.10.57)

One should diligently perform the cooking in a swinging vessel (dolāpāka), the application of the perfected powder (siddhacūrṇa), and heating in an earthen pot (bhūdharapācana) until the [substance] reaches a state of hardness. Āk 1.10.58.
The pill called Vajreśvarī, when placed in the mouth, bestows all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhi*).
As before, the transference (*krāmaṇa*) should be performed; the mercury pervades the body. (Āk 1.10.59)
(8. Mahāvajreśvarī Ghuṭikā) Pure gold, vajra-ash, iron powder, and mica—these four in equal parts, along with lead, should be placed in a crucible, sealed, and smelted. (Āk 1.10.60)
O Beloved, having again taken that [substance] from the crucible smeared with the union of the couple, one should blow upon it once more until it has become unified within the crucible. Āk 1.10.61.
One should repeatedly add purified mercury and honey in very small quantities at a time;
one should continue this until only the diamond and gold remain, and then extract them. (Āk 1.10.62)
In this [crucible], having smeared it with the powder of *vyomasattva* and *nāga* as before, one should seal it by means of the *dvandvamela* and blow it strongly with a bellows. (Āk 1.10.63)
Having gathered it into a single mass, one should blow upon it openly in a crucible until only gold and vajra remain; then one should take that up again. Āk 1.10.64.
One should repeatedly process iron filings, mica, and lead according to the previously described sequence of application, along with purified essence of honey-ore (*mākṣika*). (Āk 1.10.65)
Having repeatedly cast it out, one should blow upon it; thus, the external [substance] becomes sixfold.
This supreme seed of the Vajra is to be digested for the sake of alchemical elixirs (*rasarasāyana*). (Āk 1.10.66)

O Dear One, having processed the diamond-seed (vajrabīja) equal in measure to garlic within the mercury in its presence, one should gradually transfer it starting from the sixty-fourth part. Āk 1.10.67.
In this manner, one should grind the seed of the thunderbolt (vajra) equal in measure to the processed mercury in a heated mortar with the group of acidic substances for three days. Āk 1.10.68.

That becomes a paste (piṣṭi), which is the elixir (sūta); one should collect that paste. [The process involves] cooking in a swing (dolāpāka), anointing with the perfected powder (siddhacūrṇa), and the sealed crucible (sampuṭa) and earthen vessel (bhūdharayantra). (Āk 1.10.69)
One should perform everything as before until it attains hardness;
this pill, known by the name Mahāvajreśvarī, bestows spiritual accomplishments. (Āk 1.10.70)

When [the mercury] is placed in the mouth, the transmutation (*krāmaṇa*) should be performed as before; thus the mercury transmutes. (9. Vajrakhecarī Pill) When the mercury has been made into a mouthpiece, the seed-syllable of the Vajra of Space, equal in measure to the mercury, [should be added]. (Āk 1.10.71)
Each [of the ingredients] should be digested separately, starting from sixty-four parts;
for this mercury that has been digested, an equal amount of the seed of diamond and mica [is added]. (Āk 1.10.72)
One should grind it firmly for three days with the group of acidic substances in a heated mortar;
that becomes a *rasa* (mercury), and that *piṣṭi* (paste) should again be treated as before, O Dear One. (Āk 1.10.73)

One should repeatedly apply swinging (dolāsveda), the application of perfected powder (siddhacūrṇa), and heating in an earthen vessel (bhūdharapācana) until the [substance] reaches a state of firmness. Āk 1.10.74.
A divine pill is produced; its name is Vajrakhecarī.
When held in the mouth, it bestows accomplishment upon men, and the process of transference is as before, O Dear One. (Āk 1.10.75)

(10. The pill that destroys time) When the mercury has been made into a mouth [of the crucible], the seed of *kāntavajra* equal in measure to garlic (*rasona*) should be digested separately in portions starting from sixty-four parts, and so forth. (Āk 1.10.76)
The seed of this aged mercury, equal in quantity to diamond and magnetite, should be ground for three days in an iron mortar with the group of acidic substances after it has been heated. ĀK 1.10.77.

This mercury becomes a paste; one should then take that paste again. [One should apply] dolāsveda (swinging-fumigation), an application of siddhacūrṇa (perfected powder), and the saṃpuṭabhūdhara (earth-pot enclosure). Āk 1.10.78.
As long as it reaches a state of hardness, one should repeat this process again and again;
thus, an auspicious pill named Kālavidhvaṃsinī (the Destroyer of Time) is produced. Āk_1,10.79.
Situated in the mouth, this divine pill bestows success; as before, one should drink the *krāmaṇa*. (11.
Gaganeshvari Pill) When the king of mercury has been made into a mouthpiece, [one adds] the seed of diamond, magnetite, and mica. (Āk_1,10.80)
In each respective king of elixirs, the sixty-fourth part and so forth of that mercury is equal to the seed of the diamond and the seed of the cloud. Āk 1.10.81.

In a heated mortar, by grinding with the group of acids for three days, a fine paste is produced through thorough rubbing; then follows heating in a *dolāyantra*, application of the perfected powder, and sealing within a crucible (*saṃpuṭa*) like a mountain. (Āk 1.10.82)
One should practice this repeatedly until it reaches a state of hardness;
this pill of Gaganeshvari, when held in the mouth, bestows all accomplishments. (Āk 1.10.83)

As before, the transference should be performed; the mercury transits into the body. (12. Vajraghaṇṭeśvarī Ghuṭikā) When the king of mercury has been made ready, the seed of diamond and gold [is added]. Āk_1,10.84.
The sixty-fourth part and so forth should be processed separately and equally;
this seed of mercury is similar to that of gold and diamond. (Āk 1.10.85)
In a heated mortar, the mercury becomes a paste after three days with the group of acidic substances;
taking that paste again, one should prepare it as before. (Āk 1.10.86)
One should repeatedly perform the cooking in a swing, the application of the perfected powder, and the baking in an earthen vessel until it attains firmness. (Āk 1.10.87)

This Vajraghaṇṭeśvarī is indeed the pill that bestows accomplishment; when held in the mouth, she is divine and grants success. One should drink the previously mentioned *krāmaṇa* [elixir]. (Āk 1.10.88)

(13. Vajrabhairavī Pill) When the king of elixirs has been made into a mouth [of the crucible], gold, vajra, and the seed of mica should each be digested separately in equal parts, starting from sixty-four parts and so forth. Āk_1,10.89.
One should grind an amount of this mercury equal to gold, diamond, mica, and seed-mercury with the group of acidic substances in a heated mortar for three days. (Āk 1.10.90)
O Dear One, it should then become a powder; taking that again, one should perform the cooking by swinging (dolāpāka), apply the Siddha-cūrṇa, and cook it in a bhūdhara-pot. Āk 1.10.91.
As long as it reaches a state of hardness, one should perform the rite repeatedly;
then a divine pill is produced, known by the name Vajrabhairavī. (Āk 1,10.92)

Situated in the mouth, O Dear One, it is the *siddhakarī* [accomplisher of success], and the transmutation (*krāmaṇa*) is as before. When the mercury has been made into a pill (*ghuṭikā*), [one adds] iron, diamond, gold, and seed-mantras. (14. Tripurabhairavī Pill) Āk_1,10.93.
The mercury to be digested should be equal to the separate [added] mercury, starting from sixty-four parts;
likewise, the seed-materials of *kāntaloha*, diamond, and gold should be equal to the digested mercury. (Āk 1.10.94)
One should grind [the mercury] with the group of acidic substances in a heated mortar for three days;
the mercury becomes a paste (piṣṭi), which one should collect as before. Āk 1.10.95.
One should repeatedly perform the process of swinging-roasting (dolāpāka), applying the Siddha-powder, and baking in an earthen vessel (bhūdhara) until it attains firmness. (Āk 1.10.96)
A divine pill arises, named Tripurabhairavī;
when held in the mouth, it indeed bestows accomplishment (*siddhi*), and its transference is as before, O Dear One. (Āk 1.10.97)

(15. The Great Bhairavī Pill) When the mercury has been made into a mouth [of the crucible], the seeds of iron, diamond, mica, and gold—each equal in measure to the mercury—should be digested [into it] starting from a sixty-fourth part [of the mercury]. Āk_1,10.98 //

One should grind the seeds of space and the other elements together with this aged *sūta* (mercury) in a heated mortar (*taptakhalva*) using the group of acidic substances (*amlavarga*) for three days. (Āk 1.10.99)

The mercury becomes a paste; one should take that paste again and perform cooking in a *dolāyantra*, apply the *siddhacūrṇa* ointment, and place it in a crucible (*saṃpuṭa*) within an earthen vessel (*bhūdharayantra*).
As long as it reaches the state of hardness, one should perform the rite again and again;
this pill, known by the name Mahābhairavīya, bestows all accomplishments. Āk 1.10.101.
One should hold that in the middle of the mouth; as before, one should drink the *krāmaṇa* [elixirs].
(The *krāmaṇas* are:
*triphalā*, *musalī*, *muṇḍī*, *bhṛṅgarāja*, and *vākucī*. (Āk 1.10.102)
Nīlī, kanyā, kākamācī, hayagandhā, śatāvarī, uttarā, vāruṇī, devadālī, citrā, and punarnavā. (Āk 1.10.103)
Nirguṇḍī, sahadevī, rudantī, gajakarṇikā, bhūtāvarāta, bhallātaka, ākatuṇḍa, and amṛtālatā. (Āk 1.10.104)
Palāśa, kukkurūṭa, the juice of dhātrī fruit, milk, palāśa seed-oil, ghee, honey, and auspicious water. (Āk 1.10.105)
The marrow of the *bilva* fruit, oil, and oil derived from *jyotiṣmatī*—these indeed are the medicinal substances suitable for causing [the medicine] to permeate. (Āk 1.10.106)

These five, as declared in the half-verse, are to be employed for the purpose of transmutation (krāmaṇa), in the application of mercury-ash (rasabhasma), in the preparation of pills (guṭikā), and in the practice of alchemy (rasāyana). Āk 1.10.107.
(The fruit of the fifteen pills:
O beloved, hear the fruit of the fifteen pills: a pill fashioned from the seed of *abhra* (mica) combined with mercury. (Āk 1.10.108)
O Supreme Goddess, if it remains in the mouth for twelve years, it destroys all diseases; such a man shall live for a hundred years. (Āk 1.10.109)
A pill fashioned from the seed-syllable of Kānta and combined with mercury, when placed in the mouth, O fair-faced one, destroys all diseases for twelve years. (Āk 1.10.110)

Producing the firmness of the bodily constituents and bestowing a lifespan of a thousand years, this auspicious pill of mercury, fashioned from the seeds of lovely clouds, is proclaimed by the Rasas. Āk 1.10.111.
Remaining within the mouth for twelve years, it destroys old age and disease;
it bestows a divine lifespan of ten thousand years and increases great strength. (Āk 1.10.112)
A pill of mercury joined with gold seeds, when placed within the mouth, removes wrinkles, gray hair, and diseases from the body for twelve years. (Āk 1.10.113)
This meritorious pill, which bestows longevity and the strength of ten thousand elephants, is composed of gold, clouds, and seeds, combined with mercury. Āk 1.10.114.
It bestows a lifespan of ten million years for as many years as there are suns situated in the mouths;
it generates divine intellect and grants divine being. (Āk 1.10.115)
A pill prepared from *kānta* iron and gold seeds along with mercury, when held in the mouth for twelve years, increases one’s lifespan to ten million years. (Āk 1.10.116)
Producing great splendor and enabling the vision of treasures, subterranean caverns, and so forth, this pill—composed of lovely clouds and gold and joined with mercury—is [the means]. Āk 1.10.117.

When placed in the mouth, she grants a lifespan of one billion years until the end of twelve years; she bestows the state of a sky-walker (*khecara*) and the power to bring about universal dissolution, such as that of *Hālāhala* poison and other forces. (Āk 1.118)
The auspicious pill of mercury, joined with the liberated vajra-seed, when placed in the mouth, bestows all worldly attainments until the end of twelve years. (Āk 1.10.119)
As long as the ground is very firm, life is prolonged;
a youth is always full of desire and capable of sexual union with beloved women. (Āk 1,10.120)
A pill fashioned from vajra, clouds, and seeds, and filled with mercury, when kept in the mouth for as many years as there are grains of mercury in it, bestows all accomplishments. (Āk 1.10.121)
The Lord, who bestows long life upon men and creates the world in due order, is worshipped by the gods like Brahmā himself, having mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas. Āk 1.10.122.
He who travels through all worlds is served by Sarasvatī and Sāvitrī;
for he is endowed with the eight supernatural powers, O Goddess, beginning with *aṇiman*.
A pill prepared with mercury and the seed-syllable of Vajrakāñcana, when held in the mouth, bestows upon men the lifespan of Viṣṇu for twelve years. (Āk 1.10.124)
And he attains the state of Viṣṇu, capable of protecting like Viṣṇu;
endowed with prosperity and great strength, he is served by Sanaka and the other sages.

O beloved, this pill, fashioned from the seed-syllables of the golden cloud and the vajra, moves according to one's own will and is always served by the immortals, such as Mahendra and others. Āk 1,10.126.
O fair-faced one, when accompanied by *pārada* and held within the mouth for twelve years, it bestows the lifespan of Rudra upon men; indeed, it grants the state of Rudra itself. (Āk 1.10.127)

He is the destroyer of the world like Rudra, and he is served by Viṣṇu, Indra, and others; endowed with the powers such as atomization (aṇimā) and the rest, he is omniscient and travels to all worlds.
Endowed with divine power, he is served by the foremost of the Pramathas;
the wise one, possessed of great splendor and great strength, is meditated upon by the lords of yogis. (Āk 1.10.129)
A pill prepared from the seeds of *kānta*, gold, and diamond, combined with mercury, when kept in the mouth for twelve years, bestows success upon men. (Āk 1.10.130)
A human being attains the lifespan of a lord and the power of moving through the sky; honored by Brahmā, Indra, and the other gods, he can even make himself invisible to the world. (Āk 1.10.131)
Resembling ten million suns and possessing the strength of a great wind, he will certainly not meet destruction even at the time of the end of a great kalpa. (Āk 1.10.132)

With his soul intent on the play of yoga, he is meditated upon by the foremost knowers of yoga as being composed of the essences of the seeds of the beloved, the clouds, gold, and diamonds. (Āk 1.10.133)
O Bhairavī, he who has twelve pills (*ghuṭikā*) placed in his mouth shall possess the lifespan of Sadāśiva and become a lord who bestows grace upon all. (Āk 1.10.134)
He attains the state of Sadāśiva and likewise becomes the sovereign of the gods;
he is fire within fire, water within water, and the essence of wind within the wind. (Āk 1.10.135)
On earth he becomes the form of earth; in the void, he becomes the essence of the void.
The moon, fire, and sun are his eyes, and Brahmā, Indra, and the others are his servants. (Āk 1.10.136)
The singers were Nārada and others, and the dancers were the celestial nymphs; by his command alone were Brahmā and Indra, the creators, sustainers, and destroyers of the world. (Āk 1.10.137)
Śiva is existence-consciousness-bliss, omnipotent, all-pervading, omniscient, endowed with the supreme power (parā-śakti), meritorious, free from illusion, partless, and supreme. (Āk 1.10.138)
Thus, O beloved, have the qualities of the pills been described by me;
moreover, the power to paralyze weapons exists within all of them. (Āk 1.10.139)
O Maheśvarī, this [mantra] is the bestower of success for every elixir (*rasāyana*).
(Regarding the application of the mantra for the perfection of the pill:
This king of mantras, which grants all accomplishments, shall now be declared. (Āk 1.10.140)
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, O Amṛteśvarabhairava, make [this] nectar! To Amṛteśvarabhairava, Huṃ! Sauḥ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Huṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! Sauḥ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ!
By means of this mantra, a person shall swiftly attain accomplishment. Āk 1.10.141.
Āk, 1, 11 (The attainment of a divine body even while living; the elixir that ends death in the past).
Śrī Bhairavī said:
"O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O Maheśvara, you have now described the divine elixirs that grant spiritual accomplishments."
O Lord, O Supreme Sovereign, how is it that these [practices], which indeed grant success after a long time for bodies and aeons, may instead yield immediate success? Āk 1.11.2.
Tell that [remedy] for those whose limbs are deficient, excessive, or wasted;
and also for those who are stammering or mute, as well as for the hunchbacked and the lepers. (Āk 1.11.3)
And for those who are blind, lame, or weak, whose bodies are worn out by old age, who are always afflicted by disease, emaciated, and of wandering mind; (Āk 1.11.4)
It bestows the perfection of the body upon men who, though afflicted by spirits, ghosts, demons, epilepsy, or madness, remain with their lives intact through mere negligence. (Āk 1.11.5)
The illustrious Bhairava said: "Having heard those words of Bhairavī, you have asked well, my dear.
O lady of beautiful countenance, I shall likewise explain to you the perfection of the body."
O Dear One, five pills composed of the five elements should be prepared; the sixth pill, joined with the *piṇḍakoṣṭha*, should consist of the individual soul (*jīvātman*). (Āk 1.11.7)
But when a maiden at the proper time engages in sexual union, the blood situated in the male organ becomes semen, which is of the nature of space (vyoma). Āk 1,11.8.
The feces of her newborn son would consist purely of the principle of air (māruta), while her blood would consist of the principles of fire (tejas) and self-nature (sattva). Āk 1,11.9.
The blood of that offspring is proclaimed to be the water element; the entire body of his son is said to be the earth element. (Āk 1.11.10)
O Dear One, the essence of mercury (jīvatattva) consists of mercury, its attendant, and white [sulfur];
one should employ mercury that has the power to pierce through a crore [of layers] in measures of one karṣa each. Āk 1.11.11.
One should rub those [substances] individually within each of the single principles;
having formed pellets from them, one should set aside six types of rasa separately. (Āk 1.11.12)
The height of the human body is one cubit, while its length is half of that;
the cauldron made of copper has a thickness of six finger-breadths. Āk 1.11.13.
One should properly hold the four-faced chamber above that with the cauldron steady; O beloved, one should fill its interior. Āk 1.11.14.
Cow’s ghee and great oil—these two in equal parts—one should worship the guardians of the ten directions, the yoginīs, and the kumārikās. (Āk 1.11.15)

[One should worship] the venerable Guru, the Siddhacakra, Bhairava, as well as Bhairavī, the Lord of the Gaṇas (Gaṇādhipa), the Protector of the Field (Kṣetrapāla), and likewise one's own chosen deity. Āk 1.11.16.

[He should worship] the nine planets, the sacrificial fires, the brahmins, the astrologers, the best of physicians, as well as those who create obstacles, and the bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas. Āk 1.11.17.
One should gratify the yakṣas, rākṣasas, and gandharvas, as well as those who know mantras and one's own kinsmen, with liquor and meat, as well as with clothing, ornaments, and gold. (Āk 1.11.18)

One should cast offerings in the various directions with divine substances that are pleasing to each [deity], and one should blow [the fire] with four bamboo tubes using a fire of khadira wood. Āk 1.11.19.
When it becomes free of froth, free of smoke, and thoroughly heated, [one perceives] the venerable Guru, one's own deity, and the moon, sun, fire, and stars. (Āk 1.11.20)

Having paid homage to the worlds, one should cast the body into the cauldron; once the earthly essence known as the body is known to have been properly dissolved, one should cast in the mercury. (Āk 1.11.21)
One should blow [the crucible] intensely with effort until that paste becomes [consistent]; then, one should add the mercury known as *aptattva* and bring it to a state of redness. (Āk 1.11.22)

Afterwards, one should cast the essence of the fire-principle (tejas-tattva), which then attains the state of flesh; one should then cast the essence known as the air-principle (vāyu-tattva) into that. (Āk 1.11.23)
It attains a bright white color, and from that, the element of space (ākāśa-tattva);
O Pārvatī, one should then deposit the so-called life-principle (jīva-tattva) and the element of taste (rasa-tattva). Āk 1.11.24.
One should cast mercury into purified gold so that it becomes equal [in weight] to it;
having become endowed with life (*sajīva*), it becomes perfected (*siddha*); one should then utter the three *huṃ* syllables. (Āk 1,11.25)
He whose splendor was like the risen orb of the sun, possessed of great intelligence and prowess, a massive body and great majesty, and the immense strength of ten thousand elephants. (Āk 1.11.26)
Rich in beauty comparable to Manmatha, equal to Vāgīśvarī in speech, equal to Brahmā in intellect, glorious like Viṣṇu, and like Kubera in wealth. (Āk 1.11.27)
In renunciation and in wrath he is the fire of time; in profundity he is the great ocean;
